To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetically engineered pig kidneys can support baboon life for >1 year, and the grafts can be immunologically accepted for >6 months.
genetically engineered pig kidneys can support the life of a baboon for >30 days.

the baboon is the ideal animal model to study xenotransplantation, because it has the largest body mass, the most similar anatomy and physiology, and the longest life span of any nonhuman primate species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the treatment of chronic kidney disease, which involves the use of genetically engineered pig kidneys as a source of organs for human transplantation.
the development of genetically engineered pigs that can serve as organ donors for humans.
the development of a novel, genetically engineered pig model for xenotransplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pig-to-primate xenotransplantation model is still in the early stages of development.

the results of the studies of genetically engineered pig kidney transplantation in baboons are encouraging and promising, and that further studies are needed to evaluate the potential of this model for clinical application.
there is a significant risk of transmission of zoonoses to humans from pig‐to‐human xenotransplantation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of genetically engineered pig kidneys for life-supporting renal transplantation in baboons is feasible.
we have been able to achieve long‐term survival of genetically engineered pig kidneys with life support in baboons for >1 year.

the immunological and physiological observations made in baboons with genetically engineered pig kidney xenografts have been consistent with the hypothesis that the grafts were not rejected and functioned well because the baboons were tolerant of the grafts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetically engineered pigs can be used as a source of kidneys with the potential for life‐supporting function for up to 1 year in baboons.
genetically engineered pig organs can be transplanted into nonhuman primates with prolonged survival.
genetically engineered pig kidney transplantation can be successful in the baboon model.
